$18/hour x 40 hours x 52 weeks is "closer to $37,000 a year"

financial_checks.result: Gross $1,440; $1,140 net implies 20.8% withheld. Plausible; withholding is not sourced.

financial_checks.claim: $773/month into an index fund at ~10% grows to "close to $150,000 in 6 years"
financial_checks.result: CONTRADICTED: $55,656 contributed; about $75,840 at 10%/year compounded monthly.
About $34,800. Cannot account for $740K; remainder is unspecified.

financial_checks.claim: $40 "out of every paycheck" versus the Roth comparison of "$40 a week"
financial_checks.result: Illustrative cadence differs from the protagonist's $40 per paycheck: the banker's hypothetical is $40 a week for 10 years. $40/week for nine years at 10% is about $30,200.

financial_checks.claim: Apprentice $18-$20 is "close to half" of journeyman pay; $30 is "almost double" first-year pay
financial_checks.result: 60-67% and 1.67x respectively against the quoted $30 national median; Rey's own rate is never stated.

financial_checks.claim: Median licensed electrician about $30/hour, "a little over $62,000"
financial_checks.result: BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook: median $62,350 (May 2024), $29.98/hour. Holds.

financial_checks.claim: Electrician jobs "growing faster than almost any other occupation"
financial_checks.result: BLS projects 9% growth 2024-34 ("much faster than average"); "faster than almost any other" is not supported by that source and overstates a 9% rate (comparison with other occupations is recall).

financial_checks.claim: Self-employment tax 15.3% (both halves); estimated payments four times a year
financial_checks.result: Matches statutory 12.4% + 2.9%; not re-verified against a source this session.

financial_checks.claim: Average student borrower ~$38,000 at a little over 6%; new-vehicle payment ~$773 near national average; 8,000 hours before the journeyman exam; $50 LLC fee
financial_checks.result: Not re-verified. Apprenticeship hours, LLC fees and contractor-licensing rules vary by state; a journeyman taking independent paid jobs may need a contractor licence, which the video does not mention (state-specific; not verified).

strengths: Concrete, emotionally credible scene-first writing with a consistent foil that makes the contrast personal.
Honest closing disclaimer that $740K is not typical and luck contributed.
Plain-language tax and Roth explanations inside the story.
weaknesses: Headline truck-versus-index-fund figure ($150K) is about double the correct value.
$740K outcome cannot be derived from stated inputs.
Apprentice-to-journeyman ratio contradicts the video's own $30 rate.
No call to action; promise only implied in the first 30 seconds.
Thumbnail (self-employed van life, schedule clipboard) differs from the salaried-apprentice story for most of the runtime.
contradictions: Illustrative "$40 a week" (banker's 10-year hypothetical) versus the protagonist's "$40 out of every paycheck"; the $30,200 figure assumes 9 years where the banker said 10.
Apprentice $18-$20 versus the $30 median: 60-67%, not "close to half" (Rey's own rate is never given).
"Faster than almost any other occupation" versus BLS "much faster than average" (9%).
improvement_opportunities: Replace the $150K claim with the computed ~$75,800 (or state the rate that would produce $150K) and show it on screen as a two-line comparison: $55,656 in, ~$75,800 out.
Add a one-screen ledger for the $740K total (retirement, business equity, savings) so the reveal is derivable or label it explicitly as an illustrative composite.
State the promise in the first 30 seconds as a number ("$103,000 of tuition versus $37,440 of apprentice pay") to turn the scene into a question the viewer is waiting to see answered.
Add a state-licensing caveat before the side-job act, and one end-of-video next step.
